legend: Define the permutation scaling of an array [B1,B2,…,Bm]$$$[B_1, B_2, \dots, B_m]$$$ as the unique permutation P$$$P$$$ of [1,2,3,…,m]$$$[1, 2, 3, \dots, m]$$$ such that for each pair of indices 1≤i<j≤m$$$1 \le i  \lt  j \le m$$$, Pi<Pj$$$P_i  \lt  P_j$$$ if and only if Bi≤Bj$$$B_i \le B_j$$$. For example, the permutation scaling of the array [2,1,1,5,8,3]$$$[2,1,1,5,8,3]$$$ is [3,1,2,5,6,4]$$$[3,1,2,5,6,4]$$$.

There are n$$$n$$$ sets of integers S1,S2,…,Sn$$$S_1, S_2, \dots, S_n$$$. An array [A1,A2,…,An]$$$[A_1, A_2, \dots, A_n]$$$ is formed by choosing one element from each set, that is, Ai∈Si$$$A_i \in S_i$$$ for i=1,2,…,n$$$i = 1, 2, \dots, n$$$.
How many ways are there to choose the elements such that the permutation scaling of A$$$A$$$ is lexicographically maximal?
input: The first line of input contains an integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤5×105$$$1 \le n \le 5 \times 10^5$$$).

Then the descriptions of S1,S2,…,Sn$$$S_1, S_2, \dots, S_n$$$ follow. The description of each set Si$$$S_i$$$ contains two lines. The first line contains an integer ki$$$k_i$$$, the size of Si$$$S_i$$$ (1≤ki≤5×105$$$1 \le k_i \le 5 \times 10^5$$$). The second line contains ki$$$k_i$$$ distinct integers s1,s2,…,ski$$$s_1, s_2, \dots, s_{k_i}$$$, the elements of Si$$$S_i$$$ (1≤sj≤109$$$1 \le s_j \le 10^9$$$).
output: Print one integer — the number of ways. Since it can be very large, output it modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$.
note: In the second example, the lexicographically maximal permutation scaling is [2,1,3,4]$$$[2, 1, 3, 4]$$$ and there are 3 different ways to choose the array A$$$A$$$: [2,1,3,5]$$$[2,1,3,5]$$$, [2,1,3,6]$$$[2,1,3,6]$$$ and [2,1,3,7]$$$[2,1,3,7]$$$.
